task: The selected switch port connects to a router that does not negotiate DTP. Configure the switch port as a static trunk.

teaching.hint: The required link mode must not depend on the peer negotiating.
teaching.takeaway: Static trunk mode supplies the intended local mode. Match native and allowed VLAN settings with the peer and verify the operational state.

task: Both ends use the default untagged-native behavior. On this selected trunk, match the peer’s agreed native VLAN 99.

teaching.hint: Ordinary untagged ingress belongs to the native VLAN.
teaching.takeaway: Configure the same native interpretation at both ends. A mismatch can classify untagged traffic into different VLANs even when tagged traffic still works.

task: The approved new trunk must carry exactly VLANs 10, 20 and 99. Replace its allowed list with that complete set.

teaching.hint: Here the requirement is replacement, not addition.
teaching.takeaway: A bare allowed-list command replaces the previous list. Use it only when you intend that complete set; otherwise existing working VLANs can be removed.

task: This trunk already carries VLANs 10, 20 and 99. Permit VLAN 30 as well while preserving every existing allowed VLAN.

teaching.hint: Choose the list operation that extends the current set.
teaching.takeaway: Adding VLAN 30 preserves the existing entries. VLAN 30 must also exist, be permitted at the far end and be forwarding before its traffic can cross.

task: VLAN 20 is being retired from this trunk. Remove only VLAN 20 and preserve all other allowed VLANs.

teaching.hint: Change one member of the set without replacing the set.
teaching.takeaway: Removal affects this trunk’s permitted VLANs. It does not delete VLAN 20 from the switch database or reassign its access ports.

task: The selected port is already a static trunk to a peer that does not use DTP. Stop sending DTP negotiation messages.

teaching.hint: Trunk mode and negotiation-message transmission are separate settings.
teaching.takeaway: Suppressing DTP does not configure the far end or stop 802.1Q tagging. Keep static trunking and matching VLAN settings on both peers.

task: A VLAN works locally but fails across the interswitch link. Display operational trunks with their native, allowed, active and forwarding VLAN lists.

teaching.hint: Choose the trunk view that separates permission from effective forwarding.
teaching.takeaway: An allowed VLAN can still be absent, inactive or nonforwarding. Compare the relevant lists at both ends before changing configuration.

task: Gi0/1 is missing from the operational trunk list. Display its detailed administrative and operational switchport settings.

teaching.hint: A missing operational entry is a reason to inspect the named port’s configured mode.
teaching.takeaway: Compare administrative intent with current operation. The port may be configured as a trunk yet lack an operational link; do not change its VLAN list without that distinction.

task: VLAN 30 appears in the trunk’s allowed list but not its allowed-and-active list. Display the local VLAN database summary before editing the trunk.

teaching.hint: Permission on the trunk does not create the VLAN.
teaching.takeaway: Check whether VLAN 30 exists and is active locally, then check the peer. Repeating an allowed-list command cannot create a missing VLAN database entry.
